We're already in the `Exited` Event so this call is redundant:

> There are two ways of being notified when the associated process exits: synchronously and asynchronously. Synchronous notification means calling the WaitForExit method to block the current thread until the process exits. Asynchronous notification uses the Exited event, which allows the calling thread to continue execution in the meantime. In the latter case, EnableRaisingEvents must be set to true for the calling application to receive the Exited event.

https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.process.exited?view=net-7.0

Pretty sure this is still needed when using async IO. It guarantees that stdout and stderr are done.

You can see from the test output that the text "No templates or subcommands found matching:" was output, however the test threw on the check for that exact string:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/fb1e6a74373f1e4f09cc1b0adaac5f0535e5f07d/src/ProjectTemplates/Shared/TemplatePackageInstaller.cs#L149-L151
This implies a race condition where the process exits and we grab the output before the stdout/stderr completed writing.
